What is the optimal experience a customer should have after a popup opt-in? 

And how does that change during the holidays? 
This newsletter is a warning ⚠️ 

I see hundreds of brands make big mistakes with their post-popup experience every year. 

Their customers sign up for popups (great), but then the emails & education that comes after feels like it hurts more than it helps. Incorrect offers during sales, incorrect products being shown, etc. 

Not this year though. 

Use these tactics below to optimize your customer journey during the holidays. 

They are easy to implement and high ROI. 

Truly a no-brainer. 

5 Tips to Enhance the Post-Popup Experience 

Alia Journeys 
"Wow great. The Alia guy shilling his own software in his newsletter." 

Ok hear me out. We wouldn't have built this unless we believed it could make money for brands. And it sure does. 9-figure brands routinely send me emails thanking us for this feature. 

So here's the magic behind it. 

By now, we've all seen the power of questions in pop-ups and how much they can lift opt-in rates. 

Our team looked at these numbers and said, "Hey, why don't we just keep asking questions after the purchase experience?" 

So that's exactly what we did. 

After someone fills out a pop up, we allow brands to continue to ask customers questions that achieve a few things: 

Subconsciously guide the user along their education experience, asking them questions about their pain points that make the solution they want more and more obvious 
Using questions to filter out products they don't want and identifying products they do want behind the scenes (like a mini automated CRM for each customer) 
Surfacing products & offers relevant to them at the end of the experience 
Gathering first-party data about them along the way to inform you on future product launches, features, offers, and more. 

TLDR: Think of it like your customers skipping the entire purchase education and navigation process on your site, and instead asking customers questions that lead them directly to the product they want. And when they get there, it feels like an "Aha!" moment for them. All the questions they just answered converge into a product. clicks add to cart 

Our team routinely sets these up for brands. Whether you're on Alia or not, to learn more. There's a demo link on the page, you can book a 15-minute call with me for free, and we can riff on how this would look for you. What about Flow-verlap? 

Do you ever shop from a brand that's running a big sale, and then get a browse abandon or abandon cart email from them with their worse evergreen offer? 

To avoid this happening to you, take the dynamic sale banner I mentioned above and tweak it a bit. 

Mention that this is the best offer you have right now. Have this banner only run on flows that call out a discount already. 

When that customer opens the email, they're expecting a lower offer, but what they actually get is your most recent BFCM offer, which will surprise them for the better. 

It's not quite bulletproof though. If you're operating a bigger 8 or 9-figure brand, it's worth reviewing all your subject lines and flows ahead of the holidays and making sure this is all thought through to minimize confusion. 

Update, don't remove, your popups during BFCM 

Instead of shutting down your pop-up to avoid confusion during your sale, create a pop-up that calls out the sale. 

Offer to give people the BFCM discount and send them curated product ideas right to their inbox. 

You could even sweeten the deal by telling them you'll keep them in the loop on holiday releases and future exclusive email-only offers. 

We've got a whole article dedicated to popup ideas for BFCM . (https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ls/click?upn=u001.p25vHRhRfK3hICBtpbDyiSJ7-2BVE-2FJLnhkKtk18Em5S9i2H-2FNfCDZEkN-2B9wDkUqevk4GfdMVJs6T6p3lw1Uec-2FraB3zEzSu43RMN7KoC8MZValSauu8AcPC1U7-2BtSWx3AEdVN_fSYhS-2FaCvmmcUupDlCG63uSwgusdZE-2BuLXiJ1hkd7-2F-2FE5ue-2FDDZMoKaLASHx1Lm3uhq5iyZNub52qrEJhaXSpogcsLcURG5c0F45HSVcBMf6CSjkv4BPdKc2nKV56au8fXsaGg506jgkyEAm2e6dIacdZqRseRuWFi2PIt4gXKtZmFQIKFQE2grxW1aVOJ2vBJtle81HLh3kM7tkPqQVY4Do3Ju-2BM4z-2BGgUp83uUBej3P-2Fefm2OG32Y1KTLnCyfOlmFeVcvtEEEiaxnNofWART6m5euKSaeH6OYL1yodH51Y-2BCDDxa8hpToaL-2Bi6jW5u-2BxroAjG4vEFYaLYuBoRdTEIRdHoOZry8sznSstLV-2F3V7FkdlHZVGNEPjZ1-2ByTfesnut7yaA0agwfFbZO9U1KnaiFJjtqpVT7mSiAg78lL19Dr79JOAvt4TBieJYhS4Vi4iQ3etBv1FzJ3mcUvolu1FYlGSnHFmU5nT0yF-2Fg09ynTxI4a6EOtQaC5gGoAqBwH4Cw5aAQ-2FB0TivE7E2SIh3hI12tRr7Yhzqioie8fGJtw-3D) here 

Modify the first welcome email 

If you're using Alia, you're probably asking customers a question about their experience before you get their opt-in. 

This first-party data is incredibly valuable. 

While it's probably too late to build entire welcome flows around specific avatars and hero products people are interested in, it may still be worth tweaking your first welcome email. 

Here's why: 

The holidays will be one of your biggest email acquisition periods 
Most people are shopping much faster than usual. 

And for those reasons, the first welcome email is way more valuable during this period than people realize. 

So what should you do? 

Take your first welcome email. 
Segment the journey using the first-party data you're getting from Alia or your other pop-up provider 
Tweak each email #1 to show more imagery of the product the customer is interested in, mention the problem that customer might be having and show multiple variants or tangential products that the customer might also want. 
Flow the remainder of the emails back to your regular welcome journey 

Example: I personally love when brands show me a "Best-Seller" or "Starter Bundle" that has the gift I want to give in it. If you send me personalized recommendations like this that make my gifting easy, I'm much more likely to purchase. You just made my life so easy.

90-Second BFCM Popup Guide 

Before BFCM: 

Use VIP early access emails and teaser popups to build anticipation for your BIG sale. 
Gather emails and warm up your audience ahead of launch. 

During BFCM: 
Keep popups on: Turning them off kills conversions. Your popup should match your hero offer: There's no worse feeling than clicking an ad, going to a site, and seeing a different offer popup 

Popup Design: 

Clear headline ("Up to 40% Off Sitewide") 
Simple CTA and minimal fields. 
Match existing branding (if it's been tested), but incorporate BFCM/holiday elements. 
Add a small bonus to your hero offer (extra 5% off) if pushing list growth. 
Use the same trigger you do now, if you've tested it. Consider exit, scroll depth, or a long delay if you want to be more conservative. 

Key popup tactics for max impact: 
Timing: 10–20s delay (give people time to digest what you sell), but test this! Data collection: Ask shopper intent questions; feed results into post-BFCM email/SMS follow-ups. Personalization: Consider serving different popups for new vs. returning visitors, different email segments, device types, geographies, etc. 

Sample BFCM Popup Timeline 

3–4 weeks before: Teasers/VIP early access popup → build list & anticipation 
1 week before: Countdown to offer reveal popup → final subscriber push 
During BFCM: Sitewide offer popup + cart/exit recovery popup → convert customers 
After BFCM: Cash in on collected data with retention campaigns

ABOUT ARTWEEK 
ArtWeek Park County is a partnership between the Livingston Depot, the Livingston Center for Art and Culture and the Danforth Museum of Art. This annual event is aimed at strengthening the community by engaging with the arts and celebrating its creative legacy. 
The week features signature events like artist lectures, student & adult workshops, and fine art exhibits, culminating in a LIVE auction of the region's best art.

Shoppers cross‑check, find contradictions, and bounce. Why this matters now: Multi‑site checking is the norm. In 2025, 74% of consumers say they use two or more websites to read reviews before deciding on a local business. Bad or inconsistent info costs you sales. 62% of consumers would avoid a business if they find incorrect information online (address, hours, phone, etc.). Google expects consistency. Their official guidelines: represent your business consistently with accurate address and hours—or risk edits/suspension. AI Overviews and AI Platforms are searching for content to use. When customers get generative AI results, you're not doing your business any favors with inconsistent information, or worse—negative feedback across sites. Zero‑click is here. Many decisions are made without clicking through. Your profiles are your landing pages. What to do this month (20 minutes): Lock your Source of Truth (SoT). Update the as much information as necessary on your site first—name, address, phone, hours (incl. holidays), categories/services, and URL. Most of everything else should match what's on your site. Global Carriers Increase Fees or Pause Service to US as De Minimis Ends 

The US has officially ended the "de minimis" exemption. Effective August 29th, all shipments into the US, even those valued under $800, will incur: 10-50% tariffs based on country of origin Or a flat fee of $80-$200 per parcel, depending on the average tariff rate for that country 
Carriers are responding with price increases, service changes, or complete pauses on shipments to the US: UPS added an international processing fee of $2.50 per shipment, plus a flat $10-$20 for ground packages from Canada UPS suspended UPS® Worldwide Economy DDU (Delivered Duty Unpaid) service to the United States FedEx raised their inbound processing fee from $1.50 to $2.50 per package for international shipments

Hi Crystal, 
Zero clicks are here—Google's AI Overviews are answering buyers' queries for more searches than ever, without the buyer needing to click through to any site. And your review content influences the overviews—if it's done the right way. 

What's changed (in 20 seconds) 
  * Rolled out May 2024; Google says AI Overviews help people with longer, more complex questions and then click to explore the web. 
  * Still growing, double‑digit presence. Industry tracking shows AI Overviews are exponentially growing. 
  * How it chooses sources. Google says AI features "fan‑out" across subtopics to find supporting web pages—and use the information in the summary and show those links as citations. (Google has also tested more prominent citation lists in the UI.) Your AI Overview Readiness checklist (for reviews) Goal: Influence Google AIOs with reviews, by making it dead‑simple for Google to understand, trust, and utilize your review content. 1. Get reviews across sites 
Google differentiates between reviews about your business and reviews about a product. For your overall business reviews, Google will not consider reviews from your site since they're considered "self-serving". What Google will use are reviews from third-party platforms, like Sitejabber, Google Business Profiles, BBB, Tripadvisor, etc. The best thing you can do is collect fresh, quality reviews across sites that matter to your industry, and come up with a strategy to effectively manage them. 
In your Sitejabber account, you have access to , where you can plug in sites where you have reviews, and monitor them in one place. (https://4bq9s.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/cl/f/sh/WCPzyXJTZ72ijGkqYpXLwDPFb1CyUSRe/vv9ypVOUgVkx) Data Sources 
To learn how you can automate publishing reviews across sites, you can . If you're on a paid plan, you already have access to Review Distribution! (https://4bq9s.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/cl/f/sh/WCPzyXJTZ7AVnIy6uv11hxZ2jo65kA3m/8OpSXbSmr0rb) read more here 2. Optimize product review pages on your website 
While Google won't use overall business reviews from your site, they do ingest product reviews and consider them for SEO and AIOs signals. That means getting product reviews on your pages are extremely important. Here are our tips: 
  * Put the item name/model, who it's best for, pros/cons, comparisons, and trade‑offs above the fold; support with clear headings and anchors. (Google supports pros/cons on product/editorial review pages.) 
  * Make your pages with reviews indexable, not blocked by robots, and allow snippets. Use review widgets to easily implement reviews for every product on your site. 
  * Use structured data for your product reviews to optimize the content for Google and LLMs. Out of the box review product review widgets should achieve this without extra coding for your team. 
If you don't have them yet, learn more about how you can get product reviews here 
3. Encourage review quality (what Google rewards) 
Reviews that share first‑hand experience, specifics, photos, and original insights—not thin summaries—tend to surface more. Add evidence (images, receipts, measurements). 4. Commercial data matches reality 
Keep Google Business Profile and (if ecommerce) Merchant Center data current; Google calls these out as inputs to keep aligned. 
Bottom Line 
AI Overviews aren't something you can "switch on." Invest in reviews with first‑hand specifics, evidence, clean structure, and valid markup—and you'll give Google every reason to cite you when it summarizes.
